name: Question 13
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
{y}^{″}+9y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+9 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =\pm 3\text{i},$ and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}(x)=P\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The particular solution of the inhomogeneous equation cannot be of the form $\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x$ because this is already included in the complementary function. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x),
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x)+3x(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x) \\ {y}^{″} & =6(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x)+9x(-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
6(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x)+9x(-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x)+9x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x)=6\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
-6\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+6\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x=6\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}6\beta =6\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3x) \\ -6\alpha =-12\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =2,\beta =1.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=x(2\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\operatorname{sin}⁡3x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=P\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡3x+x(2\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\operatorname{sin}⁡3x).
$$

Now let us find constants $P$ and $Q.$ 

Substituting $y(0)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
P=2.
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=5.$ First, we differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}$:

$$
{y}^{′}=-3P\operatorname{sin}⁡3x+3Q\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)+x(-6\operatorname{sin}⁡3x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡3x)
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=5$ into the above gives

$$
3Q+2=5.
$$

Therefore, $P=2,Q=1.$

So, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\operatorname{sin}⁡3x+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+x\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$

Question 13
?

Solve the initial value problem y″+9y=6cos⁡3x−12sin⁡3x,y(0)=2,y′(0)=5.

a
y=cos⁡3x−2sin⁡3x+xcos⁡3x−xsin⁡3x
b
y=cos⁡3x−4sin⁡3x+xcos⁡3x+5xsin⁡3x
c
y=2cos⁡3x+3sin⁡3x+4xcos⁡3x+xsin⁡3x
d
y=2cos⁡3x+sin⁡3x+2xcos⁡3x+xsin⁡3x
e
y=cos⁡3x−sin⁡3x+xcos⁡3x+xsin⁡3x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we need to find the complementary function yc(x), which is the solution to the homogeneous equation y″+9y=0.

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives: λ2+9=0λ2=−9

So λ=±3i, and therefore the complementary function yc(x) is yc(x)=Pcos⁡3x+Qsin⁡3x.

We now need to find the particular solution yp(x).

The particular solution of the inhomogeneous equation cannot be of the form αcos⁡3x+βsin⁡3x because this is already included in the complementary function. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form yp=x(αcos⁡3x+βsin⁡3x), where α and β are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of yp gives: y′=(αcos⁡3x+βsin⁡3x)+3x(−αsin⁡3x+βcos⁡3x)y″=6(−αsin⁡3x+βcos⁡3x)+9x(−αcos⁡3x−βsin⁡3x).

To find the values of α and β, we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation: 6(−αsin⁡3x+βcos⁡3x)+9x(−αcos⁡3x−βsin⁡3x)+9x(αcos⁡3x+βsin⁡3x)=6cos⁡3x−12sin⁡3x

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives −6αsin⁡3x+6βcos⁡3x=6cos⁡3x−12sin⁡3x.

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations: {6β=6(equating the coefficients ofcos⁡3x)−6α=−12(equating the coefficients ofsin⁡3x)

Solving this system gives α=2,β=1.

Therefore, the particular solution yp(x) is yp(x)=x(2cos⁡3x+sin⁡3x).

The general solution is given by y(x)=yc(x)+yp(x), and therefore, the general solution in our case is y=Pcos⁡3x+Qsin⁡3x+x(2cos⁡3x+sin⁡3x).

Now let us find constants P and Q.

Substituting y(0)=2 into the general solution gives P=2.

We now need to apply the condition y′(0)=5. First, we differentiate y to find y′: y′=−3Psin⁡3x+3Qcos⁡3x+(2cos⁡3x+sin⁡3x)+x(−6sin⁡3x+3cos⁡3x)

Substituting y′(0)=5 into the above gives 3Q+2=5.

Therefore, P=2,Q=1.

So, the solution to the initial value problem is y=2cos⁡3x+sin⁡3x+2xcos⁡3x+xsin⁡3x.
